summary: I has the affected person as subject, whereas III has a persuader and a persuadee. III can take ḥḏoḏe as an ordinary reciprocal object without Detransitive morphology (PrS 20/12; PrS 21/2).
I agreement may have aʕm- for the counterpart or b- for persuasive words. The amount-sufficiency construction at 52/198 is assigned sense 2 independently of the uncertain segmentation pani.

III persuasion takes zero-marked, l-marked or suffixed human objects; d-marked content clauses and bare following content occur. 107/107 explicitly combines beneficiary -lux and object -yo, broadening the documented argument frame without a new sense.

III Infectum-wa in JTM 3.2/33 describes a habitual paid persuasion procedure; gifts or bribery are means, not a separate lexical sense. The Imperativ at 53/103 and Detransitive Infectum at PrS 77/61 supply missing boxes.

III Preterit maqnaʕle u taʕlo is morphologically active even though the German makes the fox the subject of ließ sich überreden. The supplied verse alone does not fully identify the omitted persuader; retain the quotation and raise the role assignment, rather than changing its box from the translation.
No idiom or light-verb construction requires a new collocation entry. Money and gifts are ordinary inducements; reciprocal persuasion is an object construction.

At 52/198, confirm pani as b-hani and reduced qənʕat as Infectum rather than a reduced Preterit Intransitive. The sufficiency reading is secure in context, but no definitive b- government is added for sense 2.
Confirm -lle with female patient in JTM 5.2/38, -alle in 24/121, and the two suffixes in 107/107.
In PrS 80/88 (= inherited prs 234/29), is the fox the zero-marked patient of an omitted persuader, or is another construction intended? Do not infer grammatical voice from the German alone.
Confirm alternate PrS reference numbering before any citation replacement there; unlike 60/222, it is not demonstrated to be a wrong quotation.
Correct ihres to ihre before beiden Söhne.
rationale: Söhne is the plural subject of kamen and requires nominative ihre. The extra s is a grammatical typo also present in the supplied edition.
